text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis plans to meet with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Madrid to discuss security issues and economic co-operation between both countries.
- The chief of the criminal police said that Ivan Haritonov, an alleged leader of organised crime, has left for Copenhagen after being let out of jail.
- The prosecutor's office has not decided if Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans violated anti-corruption laws as new facts have come to light.
- Central bank chief Einars Repshe has asked the prosecutor's office to find out what happened to funds supposed to have repaid by state electricity firm Latvenergo to bankrupt Banka Baltija.
- Parliament's praesidium has sent a draft project adding a second part to the constitution, which concerns human rights.
- Members of markets watchdog the securities commission have a conflict of interest as they are members of institutions which the commission is supposed to supervise.
- President Ulmanis said the stability of the government was only "relative".
- Economics Minister Guntar Krasts will not take part in the global information network conference in Bonn as the government needs a quorum.
- From May 30, Latvian citizens will have visa-free travel to Bulgaria until September 30.
- Riga city council will today consider if it will provide funds for the reconstruction of the Red Army Victory Monument, hit by a bomb last month.
